Hi Karthik / Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is excited about the latency profile and the model catalog. Before we proceed with the POC, legal has a couple of short, concrete asks that we need to lock for the eval: 

1) Can Redwood provide a short, unequivocal statement that customer content will NOT be used to train or improve models (or be included in external training corpora) unless explicitly agreed in writing? We need this to show to our security and legal teams.

2) For operational logs (request traces, auth events, system debug logs): what is the default retention window for hosted accounts, and can that be shortened via configuration or contract? We also need to know what logs you can export on request (and the format) and whether Redwood can provide a deletion confirmation/certificate when requested.

I attached our short questionnaire (Acme_data_use_questionnaire.pdf) with the exact language our reviewers prefer. If you can provide a short reply we can share directly with our procurement team.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is looking to finalize the POC by end of the week.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on training usage + logs retention for POC

Alex — thanks for reaching out and for the clear questionnaire. Short answers up front, then a little more detail for procurement: 

- On training: By default, Redwood does NOT use customer content (prompts, responses, files, or uploads) to train or improve our public models. Any use of customer content for model training or fine-tuning requires an explicit, written opt-in in the contract.

- On logs/operational telemetry: For hosted (standard) accounts the default retention is 30 days for request-level traces (full request/response payloads are purged after 30 days), and aggregated usage metrics are retained up to 12 months. These defaults can be shortened as part of an enterprise contract; we can also configure shorter windows for Dedicated capacity customers.

- Export & deletion confirmations: We can export request traces and delivery logs (CSV or NDJSON) for a specified window; for customers in an enterprise plan we provide an administratively-signed deletion confirmation after we purge the specified assets. For Private / VPC deployments, customer data remains in their environment — Redwood does not access or ingest that data unless explicitly contracted for managed services.

I attached a short privacy brief and our SOC2 evidence summary for your reviewers. Marissa (legal) — looping you in to confirm the exact contractual language Acme is requesting in the questionnaire. Neha (ops) — can you confirm the steps and SLA for generating an export + deletion certificate for hosted customers?

Next steps (suggested):
- I’ll send a concise clause for procurement to insert into the SOW/contract (Marissa please advise).
- Neha, please outline the export format and estimated turnaround (we typically hit 3 business days for standard exports; deletion certificates may take up to 5 business days depending on scope).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0199

- For the deletion confirmation: procurement needs to know whether the certificate will specify which records were purged (timestamps and object ids), and whether you will provide a hash or other verification for the export prior to deletion.

- One more nuance: does the 30-day request-level retention apply to both text payloads and any file attachments customers upload to the API? If files are excluded, procurement will request a separate retention guarantee for attachments.

If you can send proposed contract language plus a brief outline of the export workflow (fields included, format, and verification) I can forward to our legal team.

Marissa — can you draft the short clause below for procurement? Acme wants something they can paste into the SOW. Also confirm whether we can include a line about attachments being treated the same as text payloads for the 30-day purge by default. If not, we need to surface that as an exception.

Proposed clause (draft for legal):
"Redwood Inference does not use Customer Content (including text inputs, generated outputs, and uploaded files) to train, evaluate, or improve its models, or to create derived training datasets, unless the Customer provides explicit, written consent. Operational telemetry collected to support service delivery may be retained for diagnostic and billing purposes for a limited retention period; Redwood will delete request-level payloads and uploaded files associated with Customer requests within 30 days by default, unless a different retention period is agreed in writing in the applicable ordering document. Redwood will, upon Customer request, export the specified logs and deliver an administratively-signed deletion confirmation documenting the assets removed."

Neha (ops) — I can confirm the export format and throughput. For hosted customers we typically produce an NDJSON export that includes: timestamp, request_id, route, model, token counts, and the request/response payload if the customer requested a full export. We can include attachment metadata (filename, size, content-type) and provide file URLs (temporarily) for retrieval. For the deletion certificate we include the export manifest (list of request_ids and timestamps) and a signed statement of deletion.

Marissa replies quickly: "Ack — will draft a contract-ready variant and feed to procurement. Recommend adding a paragraph on audit rights and MSA amendments for Dedicated/Private deployments"

Neha adds: "Ops confirms 3 business days for standard exports; deletion certificate turnaround 5 business days once scope is agreed. For attachments we recommend the contract explicitly call out file retention and deletion steps to avoid ambiguity."

Alex, Karthik — thanks for the detail. Attaching a short, contract-ready clause below that Acme procurement can paste into the SOW. Happy to iterate if your counsel wants different language.

Contract-ready language (suggested):
"Customer Content" means all text, files, artifacts, prompts, and other inputs and outputs provided to or generated by the Service under the Agreement. Except as otherwise expressly agreed in writing, Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any models or to create derived training datasets. Operational telemetry and diagnostic logs collected by Redwood for service provision shall be retained for a default period of thirty (30) days for request-level payloads (including Customer Content included in requests) and up to twelve (12) months for aggregated metrics; such periods may be shortened by mutual agreement in writing. Upon Customer's written request, Redwood will (i) produce an export of the specified logs and (ii) provide an administratively-signed deletion confirmation describing the records purged, the timestamps covered, and the identifiers included in the export."

For clarity: attachments uploaded by customers are treated as Customer Content and are covered by the thirty (30)-day default purge for hosted accounts unless otherwise specified in the ordering document. For Dedicated and Private deployments, retention and deletion mechanics should be addressed in the applicable ordering document or SOW.

Please let me know if you need a redline for your MSA or if procurement wants this inserted into a specific clause number.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
